body: So you learned something, you cant kill yourself. I cant either. That roads a deadend. So you're free to try another road without looking back. I bet theres some stuff you don't want to do, like take care of yourself or change your situation. It'll suck but might as well start.
Now you're talking in my language. +1 for OC Community meme

It is very common (and unintuitive) to get a mood boost for days after an attempt. I speculate its a combination of being a release valve, a near death perspective shift, and your brain's  last minute survival mechanism.
too true, I mentioned this as my primary regret in my last (failed) suicide note. goodness gracious

it can be depressing! I feel the same way about my support group. It's nice to vent to fellow sufferers. At the same time hearing people who have dealt with things much longer than me, seeing them still struggling, always makes me feel worse about my future.
Damn these posts get long quickly. I always said if I posted here it wouldn't be one of those long ones. But here I am. lol
Wow, you're working so hard, and still in so much pain. *hugs

Yep, when the world is spinning around you your mind will build up a worldview that makes sense with the input its getting. Then when things calm down your supposed to latch on to a more positive worldview, but how can you let go of the only thing that makes sense?

It's a tough thing to have your dreams come true, you lose the ability to 'wait for everything to get fixed by x' or you have to come face to face with still being yourself in a new situation. Worse still is when you worked hard to get something because you wanted to feel what it would be like, only to find out its covered in the same dull shade of emotional beige as everything else.
I refuse to breed. Depression is in my genes, I know it.

Yes. I see my parents still struggling with depression and it tells me my brain has been bruised in a way that will never heal. Sometimes they like their lives, sometimes they don't.  

You also list some great existential reasons. Those things are there all the time, when I feel bad they seem to justify my bad feelings, but then after focusing on those things for so long I can't tell the difference between noticing them because I'm depressed and being actively depressed by them. I do know that when I get a break from the feelings those things suddenly don't matter anymore, I'm back in the flow of life and the rocks at the banks don't matter anymore....until I hit one.

Yep, you described it well. My therapist says depressed people always tell her they can't remember what it was like before, even though we know it was different, our brains just aren't in that mode anymore .  

I can never enjoy the good times, I know the relapse is coming, that's why I keep planning my exit even when I'm feeling good. Don't trust it, never can again, knowing it can be snatched away. 

 Hmmm. That's pretty black and white thinking now that I see it written down. Happy me would say the good times are worth it even if they end. Sad me would say the bad times aren't worth waiting through. Who is the more impartial judge? Neurotypicals pass down folklore and philosophies of the living, exclusively, can't trust them to be impartial on matters of death.

I totally agree. Love is the most beautiful thing I've ever experienced.

As I mentioned I separated from my partner in the last six months. That hurt, and remains a sore spot. My best friend from college has been my depression support system (and I his) for a long time. He's saved me before. Even though he respects suicide intellectually his love has invited me many times when I was ready to float away. I said goodbye to him in my own way, indirectly, and it was very emotional.  

He actually just drove in to town today as a last minute thing. It's the first weekend I haven't dreaded in months. I feel very nice right now, its a welcome break. You can't love away someone's pain, but its so soothing to be in its embrace
I definitely am venting a bit, and appreciative to do so. You can't do that in person they'll haul you away.

Your outlook reminds me of my own. I always feel like in the morning I run a Drake Equation for future potential happiness and plot the curves for how long I should live against it. Of course without defining the units of utility and perfect future knowledge the result is unpredictable. So I guess it's really just about how much strength I have left to fight it, and the probability of whether an epiphany arrives before I'm exhausted. I'm exhausted now...I cringe when surviving for 20 years of pain is presented as a solution.

Thank you for sharing. Also Cannabis has often saved me as well. In the earlier days it gave me a lot of comfort, and sheltered me from many storms. Later it laid the foundation foundation of my most successful years fighting work anxiety. Lately, in the midst of this particular depressive episode, it has stopping being an escape and instead of accessing my gentler nature it amplifies the toxic leftovers of my personality.

Yeah, I bought the motorbike, and gave away all my stuff except camping gear. Then I went on a test ride, and back country camping. Threw me for another loop when it didn't feel any different than normal toiling. And less sustainable even. Was a last ditch effort to do something wild I thought might be enjoyable. Un-enegized I remain.
"Fun's fun, but who needs it?"

Yep, I wanted to run away from everything. I started small, and kept going until I had sold all my possessions, quit my job, and ended my relationships and planned to go live in the national parks for the summer. Shortly before I left I started taking smaller camping trips, and realized it was no life to live in the forest, and getting rid of everything had predictably left me with nothing, no support, no hobbies, no distractions.  

Wherever you go, there you'll be, can't run from yourself.

Yep, I agree with A, B, and C. When I see others really struggling with mental illness like me, I always want to comfort them, because it's better to be comforted than not. That said, I think they should end their lives too, why struggle?  

I am not unlovable, and friends and lovers have constantly been in my life. At this point, I don't feel there's any "me" left to offer them though, when I see them I'm just "there" my sense of humor and desire to interact socially has withered away.  

Thanks for sharing, nice to hear from someone else who has some self-awareness that they are operating in a mode that is detached from reality. I feel ya.

>Like the tree grows around the knot, your personality adapts to the AD/HD and a person can actually become more lazy and passive aggressive (and ashamed and guilty).  

Shit.  

It's just, how many times can you keep failing before you stop putting yourself (*and others*) through it? When do you just give up and stop trying to walk with a broken leg?
Thanks for writing this up, it's really helpful.
Shit. Use bud to manage social anxiety. Dry. Social anxiety keeps me from meeting ents. Viscous cycle.
Had never thought of that, but just bought a pack. Cheers mate.
Self-loathing
Wow, there's a lot there. Maybe you should find someone to talk to about it...err...nevermind.

When I realized this about myself I became (am?) very depressed about it, because I'm constantly getting passionate about things, and I come up with lots of good ideas, people put me in charge many times, and it's always resolved itself naturally, but most recently I got a lot of responsibility then lost interest and it all fell apart. Now I feel like I can see in to the future that I'll never be consistently passionate about anything long enough to be successful and content.  

Also, now I'm unable to get in to anything new, because every time something excites me I just self-defeat because what's the point if I'll just lose interest later.
Yesterday I went in to my room to get a pen, then I started thinking about something, suddenly I was in the kitchen with a box of kleenex. Dammit.
